incoming.explanation: The all-movable reading depends on the fact that John's own Monatiquot freehold had already been sold in February 1661/2 (braintree-community), leaving no realty to appraise.

outgoing.explanation: Separates the 'Gurney farm' tradition from the personal homestead.
Weighs the leased Tyng farm as one of two distinct parcels.
Weighs the Monatiquot freehold as the second distinct parcel.

shortLabel: Two distinct Braintree properties: leased Tyng farm vs. Monatiquot freehold
statement: John held two distinct Braintree properties in his final years — the leased Tyng farm (the future Adams seat) and his own Monatiquot-River freehold sold to Thayer in 1661/2 — so the 'Gurney farm' of local tradition and his personal homestead are separate parcels.
